articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York’s first such death in 30 years
articles.summary: LOWVILLE, N.Y. (AP) — A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the state's first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced Monday.

articles.title: Incident at University of Toronto Mississauga campus 'contained' to single residential unit, police say
articles.summary: Peel police say an incident at the University of Toronto Mississauga campus has been "contained" to a single residential unit after students were told to shelter in place on Monday night.

articles.title: Police ‘resolve’ shelter-in-place order at University of Toronto Mississauga
articles.summary: The University of Toronto issued a shelter-in-place order for its Mississauga campus on Monday night, citing reports of police activity at a student residence hall. articles.title: Hundreds of food delivery drivers protest downtown to demand dignity, fair pay from employers
articles.summary: Hundreds of delivery drivers gathered at a protest in downtown Toronto on Monday to demand that their employers provide dignity and fair pay.

articles.title: More than a meal: Seva Kitchen Canada builds community at Allan Gardens
articles.summary: Every Sunday at noon, volunteers with Seva Kitchen Canada arrive at Allan Gardens in downtown Toronto to serve fresh, hot meals. For those who gather, the weekly service also offers familiar faces, friendship and a sense of belonging. For more than 17 years, the volunteer-run initiative has supported people facing food insecurity and loneliness. Volunteers […]

articles.title: Concerns raised over excessive crowding, safety at Toronto Halloween on Church Street event
articles.summary: The Halloween on Church Street event in Toronto sees a large number of people gather downtown, but this year's event raised multiple issues.

articles.title: A West Point cadet drugged his girlfriend to force an unwanted abortion. Then he went to grad school
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — A onetime West Point cadet drugged his then-girlfriend in her barracks room, administered abortion pills to her against her will and caused a miscarriage. Then he went on to study at two Ivy League universities, starting at one of them after he pleaded guilty to assault, according to court records and a new lawsuit.

articles.summary: Toronto police are investigating after a woman was allegedly sexually assaulted by a ride share driver in downtown Toronto on Halloween night. articles.summary: A man has been arrested in connection to a sexual assault that allegedly occurred last month in the Church-Wellesley area. Toronto police say the incident happened on Oct. 19 in Church Street and Gloucester Street area. articles.title: Man charged in 401 crash in Mississauga that left 2 dead in July, OPP says
articles.summary: A Mississauga man has been charged in a crash on Highway 401 that left two people dead and three injured in July, Ontario Provincial Police say.

articles.title: Inside man or scapegoat? Defence, prosecutors make closing submissions in Pearson airport gold heist trial
articles.summary: Was a then-Air Canada employee an inside man who helped carry out one of the biggest gold heists in Canadian history, or a scapegoat exploited by a longtime friend? Those were the two competing scenarios presented to a Brampton, Ont., court Monday as prosecutors and defence lawyers made their closing submissions in the trial of Parmpal Sidhu.

articles.title: Man faces impaired driving charges after fiery crash in Whitby leaves woman dead
articles.summary: A driver is facing impaired driving charges after a fiery collision on Highway 401 on Sunday left a woman dead, police say.

articles.title: Garden suite built under new Toronto city planning rules upsets neighbours
articles.summary: Fed up with what she calls a violation of her backyard privacy, an East York woman is going public with her campaign to have new garden suites limited to just one storey.

articles.title: Woman dies in hospital after stabbing in North York, police investigate as homicide
articles.summary: Toronto police are investigating a homicide in North York after a woman died in hospital with stab wounds on Friday.

articles.title: Pickering city council returning to in-person meetings after year-long virtual shift due to threats
articles.summary: Pickering city council is set to officially return to in-person meetings in its newly renovated council chambers on Nov. 16. after conducting municipal business online for nearly two years.
